subject: SolsticeAI - Fleet scenario planning & tentative capacity hold
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SolsticeAI runway planning - need fleet scenarios

Team —

Quick note ahead of next week's pricing review for SolsticeAI (SD-4982). They just signaled a possible Q4 go-live with steady growth: roughly 250k gen tokens/day at launch, ramping to 1.2M/day over 3 months. Ben and I want to propose a conservative Dedicated pool with soft standby for the first 90 days (so we can commit an initial minimum while keeping headroom).

Ask: Monica — can you run an availability sweep for June->Sept on the us-west and us-east fleets and show a few sizing scenarios:
- Scenario A (conservative): Minimal committed GPUs to hit 250k/day with aggressive batching and caching.
- Scenario B (base commit): Support 250k -> 600k/day with steady autoscale to a 30% buffer.
- Scenario C (ramp-safe): Support up to 1.2M/day with a 45% runway buffer and standby pool for 30 days.

Include expected latency quantiles for each (p50/p95), and whether we can place a 30-day soft hold on additional nodes if inventory tightens. Attach Solstice's initial profile I exported earlier (solstice_capacity_profile.xlsx).

I know this is tight — Ben, loop in anything I missed on commercial priorities. Rishi, please flag deal constraints (SLA tiers, credits) we should plan for.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: solstice_capacity_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SolsticeAI runway planning - availability sweep results

Marissa / Ben —

Ran the sweep across the fleet. High-level summary attached; callouts below.

Summary: we have capacity to support Scenario A and B in us-west with rebalancing and scheduled maintenance avoidance. Scenario C (sustained 1.2M/day) is feasible but requires either: (1) converting ~40% of on-demand capacity to a short-term reserved pool in us-west (14 GPUs for 30 days), or (2) leveraging burst capacity in us-east with cross-region routing (higher p95 latency ~40-60ms additional).

Latency (approx, mixed model family):
- Scenario A: p50 28ms, p95 78ms
- Scenario B: p50 32ms, p95 95ms
- Scenario C (with reserved 14 GPUs in us-west): p50 35ms, p95 120ms

Soft-hold options: we can place a provisional 30-day soft hold on the 14 GPUs in us-west (mark as "standby reserve") pending contract signatures; this would require Ops approval and a small upfront reservation fee to lock inventory. If you want that, I need an explicit RFC from Sales and an approval from Capacity to avoid double-booking.

Attachments: solstice_capacity_summary.pdf (pdf), solstice_capacity_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

- Monica
Monica Patel
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@solsticeai.com>, Peter Lewis <peter.lewis@solsticeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: SolsticeAI - proposal for provisional standby reserve (SD-4982)

Alicia / Peter —

Thanks again for the detailed traffic profile last week. Internal teams ran a few fleet scenarios and we have a recommended approach to keep your launch runway protected while we finalize contract terms. High level:

1) Initial Dedicated commit sized for 250k gen tokens/day (recommended instance mix included in the attached SOW).
2) 30-day provisional standby reserve for an additional 14 GPUs in us-west that we can activate if demand ramps ahead of final sign-off. This hold requires a nominal reservation fee and an RFC from our side to Ops to prevent double-booking.
3) If you choose to finalize a 90-day commit, the standby fee will be credited toward the committed value.

Would you be comfortable with us placing a short provisional hold while you finalize procurement? Ben can follow up with pricing and the credit terms.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm you want Redwood to place the 30-day provisional hold (reply-all).
- Ben will send a short amendment showing the reservation fee and credit mechanics.
- We will open RFC with Ops to lock the GPUs in our inventory system.

Attached: Solstice_SOW_v3.pdf (scope + instance mix), solstice_capacity_profile.xlsx (profile exported). HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/SD-4982

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Solstice_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@solsticeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Lewis <peter.lewis@solsticeai.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jun 2028 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SolsticeAI - proposal for provisional standby reserve (SD-4982)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear options and for running the scenarios. We appreciate Redwood being proactive on runway risk. Solstice would like you to place the provisional 30-day standby hold on the 14 GPUs in us-west while we complete procurement. We understand the reservation fee and that it will be credited if we convert to a 90-day commit. Please proceed.

One ask: can you include the DocuSign amendment with the reservation fee terms and the credit clause? Peter and I will try to get internal approval this week.

Alicia Park
Head of Infrastructure, SolsticeAI
alicia.park@solsticeai.com
